strategic_differentiation: The proposal's research differentiation is the defensible end-to-end coupling of three capabilities the reviewed literature reports as underdeveloped in combination: (1) learned multimodal fusion of multi-source Earth observation (Sentinel-1 SAR, Sentinel-2 optical, PlanetScope high-resolution imagery, ERA5 meteorological reanalysis) and field sensors, (2) explicit probabilistic crop-water-state estimation (root-zone soil moisture and crop water status for tomato, with uncertainty carried honestly from observation through the model), and (3) water-use-efficiency-oriented irrigation decision optimisation via uncertainty-aware AquaCrop calibration and counterfactual simulation over weather ensembles. The targeted novelty occupies the single empty cell in the systematic literature review's research-gap matrix — Real-Time Decision Support × PlanetScope — argued narrowly and defended against 50 reviewed studies rather than asserted. The methodological commitment distinguishing this proposal from related work is the honest uncertainty chain from multi-sensor observation to irrigation decision: every model output reports not only what the field state is but how certain that estimate is, and that uncertainty propagates all the way into the decision. Objectives are measurable against a defined validation protocol (90% prediction-interval coverage on the validation set as the calibration criterion; Route B patch covariation proven by co-located seasonal campaign), not merely asserted. The researcher-and-host differentiation rests on a unique disciplinary pairing unavailable in a single-discipline fellowship: Dr. Rositsa Cholakova (plant physiologist, non-destructive evaluation of drought-stressed tomato plants — PhD summa cum laude 2020 — provides the biological ground truth engine, RQ4) is hosted in the geoinformatics and remote sensing group at ELTE Budapest under Dr. András Jung (remote sensing, hyperspectral imaging, field spectroscopy, multisensor-drone fusion), creating a genuine two-way knowledge transfer in which neither partner's disciplinary capability alone is sufficient for the end-to-end framework. The proposal is framed as a European Fellowship at ELTE Budapest, Hungary (intra-EU, Bulgaria → Hungary, 24 months), with Earth-observation data access confirmed (PlanetScope via Planet platform/API; Sentinel-1/2 open data; ERA5 reanalysis) and Hungarian tomato field access secured via associated partner AgroVIR. Research output is a TRL 3–4 research prototype, proportionate to a 24-month fellowship and appropriate to the novelty claim.
